revised_headline_claim: Environmental mismatch is an outcome of a multi-axis tracking system: similar low mismatch can be maintained by different allocations between movement and timing, while finite temporal capacity, spatial geometry and partner matching determine when that buffering must change or fail.
licensed_framing: low environmental mismatch can be actively maintained by compensation across spatial and temporal tracking axes
similar endpoint mismatch can arise from different movement-timing allocations under the exact local null
temporal buffering is finite and spatial tracking re-enters under stronger forcing
coordination barriers are a failure mode of reallocating tracking burden between interacting partners
small mismatch is not by itself evidence of weak environmental forcing or little adaptive response
prior_art_limits: do not claim novelty for generic mismatch buffering
do not claim novelty for integrating spatial and temporal climate responses
do not claim that all low mismatch implies high hidden cost
do not treat synthetic thresholds as empirical thresholds

added_prior_art.citation: Fredston et al. 2025, Trends in Ecology & Evolution 40:629-638
